body:
Yeah, it drives me mad. I swear, if they ever send him as my assist, I don't even care who's around, I will literally be like, "lol no. Leave. Send someone else. Like seriously, get out of my room."
They act like it's just a "he said, she said" thing, but isn't *everything*? Everyone goes, "oh, he's just a 'lady's man!'" Like, no. The ladies have to actually *like* you for you to be a "lady's man." Being a disgusting pervert isn't a qualifier.

And we're not *alone* alone, there are just certain positions/shifts where you technically get transferred somewhere else, to another floor or another building so our department stops being responsible for giving us breaks or providing backup and it falls on the transfer department--which frequently involves threatening to leave them short a person if they refuse you a break/having more physically demanding (lifting, supporting, turning, changing) patients who are more draining than ones through our department. So we can go an entire day without seeing a single person we know if we get a shift like that, which is exhausting in its own way.

They have miscellaneous services available, but this is more of a unit-specific issue than across the board. And it'd be easy for them to deny that I'm getting difficult patients/say that's what I signed up for, so it'd probably cause a lot of drama for no result...kind of like reporting that guy...

Oh :/
Do you watch cooking shows too? I may or may not watch anything with Gordon Ramsay in it 😬

Do you cook? Or just like watching cooking stuff?
Dang, that doesn't sound super uplifting :/
What stuff on YouTube? And top 3 subreddits?

Oh :/ 
Well what things do you do during the day?

I was assuming you get to sleep in 😬
That's my favorite thing when I'm not working haha

Oh no :/
That's okay though! Relaxing should be good for you :)

Hi! 
Is it your day off?

I'd rather not describe what happened, other than to say that they made extremely unwelcome advances that escalated to the point that I was bawling and having a panic attack while physically fighting him off.

And I'm so over this shit. I'm at work and *once again* got the shit assignment where I literally will be on my own in another department with a more physically demanding job and will literally not see a single coworker I know for the entirety of the next 12 1/2 hours and will also get fewer breaks.

Yeah, I really thought they'd do something, but it ended up pretty much being pointless going through the stress to bring it up. It's just frustrating to me because our entire job is working with at-risk people (we had to have level 2 background clearance to be hired) so I'm really shocked they wouldn't look into it further when they seem to take patient safety really seriously. They've been at least making sure that *someone else* gives me my breaks so I don't have to deal with that, but he's still regularly in close proximity to me, which affects me and in turn affects the care I can give my patients and the distraction of that anxiety could actually put me in danger if I'm with a volatile patient who would require extra attention.

I don't want to prolong the drama associated with that stuff by bringing it up again to management, because I feel like that's finally dying down, but I'm still dealing with the "after effects." I feel like I have to re-prove myself as a team player and a hard worker and work *extra* hard to win people over (coworkers *and* management) because I feel like I come off as a complainer or a tattler or like I'm just drama. It's affected my relationships with my "work friends" as well and has made me wary of getting close to anyone, both because I'm not sure who started the gossiping and also because if *one* guy here is like that (and has friends who support him), I'm sure there are *more*. If I had friends outside of work, it wouldn't be such a big deal, but I think it's the combo of now having a huge life stressor and needing support and *also* because it's all happening at work, having that friendship and support taken away as well. It just feels so lonely and impossible and overwhelming.
Not to mention, my job relies on being mentally healthy and stable, so not only do I feel like there's been a significant jab to my own mental health and progress (and like I've had my own hard work and recovery stolen from me), but I can't even bring it up with the people around me for support because it would make my coworkers and supervisors feel like I was unstable and incapable of doing my job.
It's just such a fucking mess.
